chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, he raised it (to the Imam) and said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of a man who married a slave-girl of a man whose master would free her upon the birth of her first child; she gave birth to twins, so he said: 'Both are freed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the emancipation of a slave-girl who gives birth to twins under the condition of freeing upon the first birth?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *Umm al-Walad* (mother of the child) in Shia jurisprudence, where emancipation is triggered by the birth of the first offspring. Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarified that the condition is fulfilled by the first birth event, thereby granting freedom to both twins born from that single instance, emphasizing the generosity inherent in manumission laws.
